title: The spec should not imply a specific point of execution of inline async module scripts that don't have external dependencies
body:
The spec [says](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-script-element:attr-script-async-8):

> For [classic scripts](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#classic-script), if the [async](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-script-async) attribute is present, then the classic script will be fetched [in parallel](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#in-parallel) to parsing and evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes).

and

> For [module scripts](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#module-script), if the [async](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#attr-script-async) attribute is present, then the module script and all its dependencies will be fetched [in parallel](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#in-parallel) to parsing, and the module script will be evaluated as soon as it is available (potentially before parsing completes).

and

> This is all summarized in the following schematic diagram:

In the diagram, async script execution starts immediately from its fetch end point without even a bit of parser timeline in between.

For external scripts, this formulation is OK enough, because Web content can't really distinguish between the parser getting interrupted immediately upon a network response completing and the parser yielding some time after a network response has been completed. The latter just looks like the network response too a bit longer.

For inline async module scripts that don't have external dependencies, the spec text appears to grant a guarantee that shouldn't actually be granted: Since inline module script that don't have external dependencies become available immediately upon their HTML end tag, the spec text seems to suggest a guarantee that such a script couldn't observe the parser having had built the DOM any further.

However, Chrome and Safari clearly don't give such a guarantee. In Chrome and Safari, the module script in this [demo](https://hsivonen.com/test/moz/inline-async-module-script-without-deps.html) consistently observes 30 div elements, although if the guarantee that the spec appears to make existed, it would always observe 0 div elements.

It would be architecturally cleaner in Gecko not to provide the guarantee that the spec text appears to provide but Chrome and Safari don't provide.

Please change the spec text to make it clear that even inline async module scripts that don't have external dependencies do not execute at a guaranteed point relative to the parse. It would be even better if the diagram showed a tiny bit of green line between the end of the blue and the start of the red both for async classic scripts and async module scripts.
